description:
Residual of the native re-green, split out of fz-go4.18.3. The keystone (fz-go4.18.3.1) de-coupled the resume-PAYLOAD shape from oscillating demand and greened 2 of 8. The remaining 6 fail at a SEPARATE convergence locus: the transport INPUT-merge / executable-MEMBERSHIP demand path, schedule-dependent non-monotonicity.

REMAINING FAILURES (at HEAD after keystone lands; 931/6)
- compiler2_native_program_adapts_delivered_calls_from_callee_return_lanes -> "native clause dispatch required omitted semantic input 1 for executable 185" (a transport INPUT shape erased, not a resume).
- compiler2_native_program_carries_published_callable_boundary_targets_into_closure_calls -> same "omitted semantic input" family.
- compiler2_native_program_jit_adapts_callable_raw_returns_back_to_value_refs -> "materialize absent value ty Ty(21) in Continuation{FnId(7), index 2}".
- compiler2_native_program_resource_fixture_shapes_callable_boundaries_explicitly -> test assertion "resource return is not transported".
- compiler2_native_program_does_not_fabricate_nil_for_zero_width_resume_payloads -> no retained zero-width continuation.
- escaping_destructor_keys_its_activation_at_the_grounded_boundary_surface -> PoisonError, full-run only = schedule-dependent.

EVIDENCE IT IS A DISTINCT LOCUS
Between two identical single-test runs the fatal SHIFTS ("missing return-flow position ExecutableReturn{...,need:Value}" <-> "omitted semantic input 1"), confirming schedule-dependent demand/membership non-monotonicity. The "missing ExecutableReturn position" is a MEMBERSHIP gap (executable/frontier flicker), not a shape gap.

SEARCH NARROWED (two loci ruled out — do NOT repeat)
- NOT record_return_demand (already monotone via join_assign).
- NOT the RuntimeDemand product reads: a monotone ExecutableRuntimeDemand::raise_to_floor (sound — derive_executable_runtime_demand reads only a target's input_demands, never callable_flows, at runtime_demand.rs:2147/2355/2485) + monotone record_latest_runtime_demand + flooring every demand read was built clean with NO regressions but was COMPLETELY INERT for the 6. The residual shrink does not flow through RuntimeDemand product reads.
- A cycle-seed floor at produce_runtime_demand_product was also inert (and a naive version regressed range_and_map_to_list by changing wait-vs-proceed flow).

LIKELY TRUE LOCUS
collect_executable_input_constraints (transport.rs:2796) — its own comment documents a known schedule-dependent non-monotone anchor/union gate — plus the demanded-executable frontier / executable-membership flicker. Fix must be correct-by-construction and PROVEN monotone (schedule-independence test, repeated/varied-order full runs), not green-once. Apply the same producer-sourced / monotone-join discipline as the keystone to the input-merge path.

SIGNAL
cargo test --lib compiler2 = 0 failed, STABLE across >=3 fresh full runs and schedule-varied drives. Then fz-go4.18.3 (umbrella) is satisfied and fz-go4.18.4 (delete spine) unblocks.

comments.text: Lead (unverified): during fz-go4.18.3.1 a MORE AGGRESSIVE variant was explored but NOT committed (it leaked into the main checkout as uncommitted changes; saved at scratchpad/stray-aggressive-resume.diff). It drops the !demand.is_callable() gate entirely and unions EVERY resume that has a local callee return position (callable returns included) with the callee ExecutableReturn, plus a debug eprintln. The keystone deliberately kept callable returns on the demand-driven path to preserve boundary selection. Whether producer-sourcing callable resume returns helps the residual 6 is UNPROVEN (the residual signatures are input-merge/membership 'omitted semantic input' + 'missing ExecutableReturn position', not resume-callable). Treat only as a possible angle; the prime suspect remains collect_executable_input_constraints (transport.rs:2796) + the demanded-executable frontier.

DIAGNOSIS (agent, no fix committed — STOPPED per protocol: root cause is NOT the scoped transport input-merge gate; it is a types/identity-layer canonicalization defect, and the 6 are at least TWO distinct loci. Bundling would violate one-ticket==one-commit).

PRIME SUSPECT collect_executable_input_constraints (transport.rs:2242) is INNOCENT. Instrumented every degenerate/Absent path; the gate never erased a shape for the failing slots.

FAMILY A — 'omitted semantic input' (compiler2_native_program_adapts_delivered_calls_from_callee_return_lanes, ..carries_published_callable_boundary_targets..). ROOT CAUSE: a NON-CANONICAL type-addressing round-trip. executable_key_for_transport_position (transport.rs:1404) reconstructs an ExecutableKey from a transport-position's ExecutableSymbol via ActivationKey::from_inputs, which CANONICALLY re-addresses the inputs. But the symbol carried in the position was minted from a real ExecutableKey whose input type is NON-canonically addressed. Proven for fn 185 input[1] = reducer-continuation union {:halt,{[T],int}} | {:cont,{[T],int}} | {:cont,{[T],int}}: symbol var addr = a1_1_0_e (no union-variant discriminator), from_inputs re-address = a1_u0_1_0_e (WITH variant disc u0) — distinct interned Ty ids (e.g. Ty(170) vs Ty(185)). ROUNDTRIP4404 MISMATCH is DETERMINISTIC when that union arises; once==twice=TRUE (from_inputs IS idempotent on its own canonical output, so the canonical form is a stable fixpoint). CONSEQUENCE chain: reconstructed seed key != the real demanded executable -> the transport-component cone (project_transport_component_product) never contains the anchor's exact executable -> shape graph never anchors ExecutableInput{sym,idx} -> build_union !contains anchor -> degenerate single-position component recorded -> produce_transport_shape_product records TransportShapeFact::Absent -> position absent from session.transport_shapes().keys() -> materialized_executable_transport omits it from input_positions -> native lower_clause_dispatch_executable (native.rs:407) hits required-but-None -> 'omitted semantic input N'. SCHEDULE-DEPENDENT because which reducer-continuation alternatives (and how many) accumulate into fn 185's input depends on wake order. NOTE: backend.rs:427 has the identical from_inputs reconstruction and is equally vulnerable.

WHY IT IS A TYPES-LAYER DEFECT: a memory invariant (fz-hwn.27 addressed-arrow unifies ActivationKey/CallableSurface) says activation-key arrows are canonical addressed arrows. The fn-185 key VIOLATES it: its input arrow is a 3-alternative union whose shared var is addressed as if single-alternative (a1_1_0_e). Some key-mint / type-join path produced a non-canonically-addressed union that the interner holds distinct from from_inputs' canonical form. Candidate: the executable key for the reducer specialization is minted when the continuation union has 1 alternative ({:cont,..} -> no Variant step -> a1_1_0_e) and the union later grows to 3 alternatives without the arrow being re-canonicalized (or a union/join builds the 3-alt arrow without per-variant re-addressing). FIX DIRECTION (correct-by-construction, identity layer, NOT transport): guarantee every ExecutableKey activation arrow is canonical so from_inputs round-trips exactly — i.e. address_inputs/union construction must produce ONE canonical addressing for a union-of-tuples with a shared var. once==twice=true means the canonical target is well-defined and stable. This is high blast radius (all activation keying, dispatch, surfaces) -> its own ticket, NOT this one.

FAMILY B — 'materialize absent value ty Ty(21) in Continuation{FnId(7),index 2}' (jit_adapts_callable_raw_returns_back_to_value_refs), 'no retained zero-width continuation' (does_not_fabricate_nil_for_zero_width_resume_payloads), 'resource return is not transported' (resource_fixture_shapes_callable_boundaries_explicitly), and escaping_destructor (full-run only). These do NOT exhibit the ROUNDTRIP mismatch (instrumented globally; zero mismatches on those drives). They fail via a SHAPE-level Nothing on a continuation/resume position (native.rs:3235 materialize Absent from a decoded Shape(Nothing)), distinct from Family A's missing-membership. This is a SECOND locus adjacent to the keystone's resume-shape territory (the keystone fixed the DATA-return resume; a callable-return continuation field / zero-width resume still collapses to Nothing).

RECOMMENDED DECOMPOSITION: (1) New ticket (identity/types layer): make activation-key arrows canonical so executable_key_for_transport_position and backend.rs:427 round-trip exactly — fixes Family A's 2 omitted-input tests; add a from_inputs(symbol.input).inputs()==symbol.input round-trip invariant test + a union-of-tuples-shared-var address canonicalization unit test. (2) Separate ticket for Family B: trace the Shape(Nothing) on the continuation/resume position (jit_adapts Ty(21), zero-width, resource) — likely a sibling of the keystone resume-shape producer-sourcing applied to callable-return continuations. Each is its own coherent convergence commit. The .18.3.2 SIGNAL (all 6 green) requires BOTH.
